findings.title: V2 `canManage()` grants group management to callers with only VIEW on all groups
findings.description: `canManage()` returns true when the caller has `VIEW` or `MANAGE` on the all-groups resource (line 70). `hasPermission(null, …)` falls back to the "Groups" type resource (lines 141-150), so a policy that grants only `view` on all groups passes. The no-arg `requireManage()` gates top-level group creation: `GroupsResource.java:181` calls it in `addTopLevelGroup`, and `GroupPermissions.requireManage()` (`GroupPermissions.java:279-283`) dispatches to this override. A view-only admin can therefore `POST /groups`. The per-group `canManage(GroupModel)` at lines 73-80 requires `MANAGE`, so the two disagree. The Javadoc at `GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:72-78` documents VIEW-as-manage, so it has to change with the code. Fix: check `MANAGE` only, and add a test that a VIEW-only all-groups policy gets 403 on `POST /groups`.

findings.title: `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` never matches per-group grants and returns a resource UUID
findings.description:
- Line 121 calls `findByType(server, "Groups", …)`. `JPAResourceStore.findByType` filters on the `type` column (lines 248-269). Group resources created by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` (lines 118-128) never call `setType`, so only the type-level resource is returned and per-group grants are never seen.
- Line 123 adds `groupResource.getId()`, the internal UUID. The resource name is the group ID (`AdminPermissionsSchema.java:118-121`). V1 correctly uses `getName()` (`GroupPermissions.java:313-316`).
- Line 122 calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), …)`, which does `findByName` on that UUID (line 141). It never matches, so it always falls back to the all-groups grant.

Effects, traced through the callers:
- **Per-group VIEW_MEMBERS only:** the set is empty, so `getUsersCount(realm, Set)` returns 0 (`JpaUserProvider.java:599-602`). `/users/count` is wrong (`UsersResource.java:425, 430`).
- **All-groups VIEW_MEMBERS:** the set is `{UUID of the Groups type resource}`. `JpaUserProvider.java:762-766` restricts results to members of that ID, so the user list is empty.
- **Per-group VIEW_MEMBERS, user search:** no restriction is applied, so DB pagination (`first`/`max`) runs before the per-user `canView` filter in `toRepresentation` (`UsersResource.java:456-467`). Pages can be short or empty even when matching users exist.

`testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers` passes only because the post-filter catches the one user. The same call is in `BruteForceUsersResource.java:147`.

Fix: set the type on group resources (or select by name), use `getName()`, exclude the type-level resource by name, and add tests for count, paging, and all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS. Consider moving the duplicated `groupIds` + `toRepresentation` logic (`UsersResource.java:445-454`, `BruteForceUsersResource.java:144-153`) into one place.

findings.title: Existing realms never receive the new Groups resource type or scopes
findings.description: `init()` returns early when the admin-permissions client already exists (lines 250-252). It runs only on realm creation (`RealmManager.java:571-572`) or when `ADMIN_PERMISSIONS_ENABLED` flips to true (`JpaClientProviderFactory.java:67-73`). This change adds `Groups` to the schema (lines 84-90) and three scopes (`manage-membership`, `manage-members`, `view-members`). Realms that already enabled V2 will lack the `Groups` type-level resource and these scopes. Creating a group permission there then fails in `getOrCreateResource` with `ModelException("No scopes found.")` (lines 123-127). No migrator is in this change. If V2 has shipped, one is needed. If it hasn't, this can be waived.

findings.title: V2 user checks drop the ADMIN role with no stated reason
findings.description: `canView(user)` and `canManage(user)` previously short-circuited on `hasOneAdminRole(ADMIN, …)` and now check only `MANAGE_USERS`/`VIEW_USERS`. `canMapRoles` and `canManageGroupMembership` (lines 76-92) changed the same way. V1 never checked ADMIN, so this aligns V2 with V1, but the diff does not say so. Removing a grant can only restrict access, so the risk is lockout of master-realm admins whose full access came through ADMIN. I did not trace the composite setup in `RealmManager.java:346-372`. Confirm with a test for a master-realm admin under V2, or restore the check.

findings.title: The new V2 paths lack tests for the cases that break
findings.description:
The added tests cover group-based user search with a per-group grant. They do not cover:
- VIEW-only all-groups → `POST /groups` returns 403 (first FAIL).
- `/users/count` and paginated `/users` for group-scoped viewers (second FAIL).
- All-groups VIEW_MEMBERS listing users (second FAIL).
- A master-realm admin under V2 (the ADMIN finding above).
- MANAGE_MEMBERS granting `joinGroup` through the new `canManageByGroup` branch in `canManageGroupMembership` (`UserPermissionsV2.java:85-92`). `testManageGroupMembership` covers only MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP.

findings.title: Group and subgroup listing lost the hoisted global-view check
findings.description: The previous code computed `canViewGlobal` once and short-circuited. The new filter calls `canView(g)` per element (`GroupResource.java:179`, `GroupsResource.java:113`). Each call runs `hasOneAdminRole`, which builds a `RealmManager` and does a client lookup (`MgmtPermissions.java:163-173`). The cost is bounded by how many elements the paged stream visits, so the impact is modest. Restoring `canViewGlobal || …` is a one-line change.

findings.title: `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` Javadoc says it returns a Stream
findings.description: The Javadoc says `@return Stream of IDs of groups with view permission.`, but the method returns `Set<String>`.

findings.title: Minor style issues in the new test code
findings.description: There is a double semicolon on `new GroupRepresentation();;`. `RealmAdminPermissionsConfig.java` also has trailing whitespace after `REALM_MANAGEMENT_CLIENT_ID, `.

findings.title: Removing the per-stream `canView` filter in `searchForUser` is safe
findings.description: The old code applied `usersEvaluator::canView` before `toRepresentation`. The new code drops that filter, but `toRepresentation` still applies it (`UsersResource.java:460`), so the check still runs per user. The pagination caveat in the second FAIL still applies.

findings.title: Listener gating and removed helpers are behavior-preserving
findings.description: Moving the `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` check from per-event to registration changes nothing, because profile features are fixed at startup. Grep finds no remaining callers of `canManageDefault()`, `canViewDefault()`, `getGroupsWithViewPermission`, or `searchGroupModelsByAttributes`. The V1 `canList`, `canView`, `canManage`, and `canQuery` role checks match the old `*Default` helpers.
